extraction.name: CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images
extraction.description: We assemble a dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed (CC) images, which we use to train a set of open diffusion models that are qualitatively competitive with Stable Diffusion 2 (SD2). This task presents two challenges: (1) high-resolution CC images lack the captions necessary to train text-to-image generative models; (2) CC images are relatively scarce. In turn, to address these challenges, we use an intuitive transfer learning technique to produce a set of high-quality synthetic captions paired with curated CC images. We then develop a data- and compute-efficient training recipe that requires as little as 3% of the LAION data (i.e., roughly 70 million examples) needed to train existing SD2 models, but obtains the same quality.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.citeAs: Gokaslan, A., Cooper, A. F., Collins, J., Seguin, L., Jacobson, A., Patel, M., Frankle, J., Stephenson, C., & Kuleshov, V. (2023). CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.16825.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We began with the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files, as well as Flickr IDs linking to the original data. We re-scraped these images from Flickr, based on the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We center-cropped and resized all of the images to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels for captioning. At training time of the diffusion model, all images remain in their native resolution.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We used a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model to produce high-quality, synthetic captions for the CC images.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Our model underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings. These categories originated from the Conceptual Captions dataset, which relies on web-scraped data. We also observed reduced diversity of n-grams in our synthetic captions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Our model underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings. The YFCC100M data is about a decade old; its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B.
